Leviathan

luh-VY-uh-thun · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Leviathan is something enormous and extremely powerful, especially an organization, vehicle, or creature.

The new aircraft carrier was a true leviathan, longer than three football fields and carrying over five thousand crew members.

Worked Example

Critics described the merged corporation as a leviathan capable of crushing any small competitor that dared challenge it.

Leviathan is used for something so massive and powerful that it feels almost impossible to resist or compete with.

How Strong Is It? — large → leviathan → colossal

large vs. leviathan

large vs. leviathan: Large is a plain, everyday word for size, without leviathan's sense of overwhelming, almost intimidating scale.

colossal vs. leviathan

colossal vs. leviathan: Colossal pushes the size even further, describing something so gigantic it seems almost impossible.

Build the Word

The pieces

origin — livyathan

origin — livyathan: a giant sea monster (Hebrew livyathan, from the Bible)

Put it together

Put it together: Leviathan comes from Hebrew livyathan, the name of a monstrous sea creature described in the Bible -- so massive and powerful that its name eventually came to describe any enormous, overwhelming thing.

Use the root in a new word: Leviathan (the book)

Use the root in a new word: Leviathan (the book): In 1651, philosopher Thomas Hobbes named his famous book about government Leviathan, comparing a powerful state to the biblical sea monster -- huge, and impossible to fight alone.
